questions.e: Production 'on speculation for an open market' and display in dining rooms rather than places of devotion are the facts the author says sit awkwardly with the sermon reading. The emblem-book verses are cited as support for the moralizing interpretation, not as a difficulty for it.
o: Many of the paintings were made for sale to buyers who had not commissioned them.
The paintings were commonly displayed in rooms used for dining.
Emblem books attached moral verses to objects like those in the paintings.

questions.s: The critics' objection to the nutrition argument is that it
questions.e: The critics say the argument 'proceeds largely by elimination' and assigns the remaining decline to diet 'without measuring diet directly.' The nutrition argument gives medicine 'little credit,' so the second choice reverses it, and the passage describes incomes as rising, not falling.
o: attributes the decline to a cause that it never directly measures
overstates the part that medical treatment played in reducing mortality
ignores evidence that incomes fell during the late nineteenth century
relies on mortality records from too few European cities to be persuasive
confuses the decline of waterborne disease with the decline of other diseases

questions.s: Which of the following, if true, would most seriously weaken the reasoning in the final sentence of the passage?
questions.e: The final sentence rules out income because it 'rose gradually' while deaths fell abruptly; if incomes actually jumped at the same moment as the new supplies, the timing would no longer separate the two causes. The point about cities growing wealthier is tempting but already conceded in the previous sentence, and it says nothing about sudden changes. Slow declines in other diseases would, if anything, support the water explanation.
o: Some cities built waterworks but did not install sewers until several decades later.
Effective medical treatments for waterborne diseases became available only in the twentieth century.
Mortality from diseases not spread by water declined only gradually over the same period.
Several of the cities that built waterworks were growing wealthier while they did so.
In the cities in question, household incomes typically jumped in the same years that the new water supplies opened.

questions.s: The author regards the comparison with lineages that do not echolocate as important because it
questions.e: Lineages that do not echolocate show how many substitutions are shared 'purely by chance,' which is the 'explicit estimate' the last sentence says any striking coincidence must be judged against. The passage states that the two groups evolved echolocation 'independently,' and some hearing genes still showed more convergence than chance, so 'none ... has any connection to hearing' is too extreme.
o: demonstrates that bats and toothed whales inherited echolocation from a single common ancestor
shows that convergence in physical form is in fact rarer than convergence in genetic sequence
supplies a baseline against which the frequency of shared substitutions can be judged
proves that none of the substitutions shared by bats and whales has any connection to hearing
explains why the earliest studies had examined only a small number of the genes for hearing

questions.s: It can be inferred from the passage that, before the studies described, many biologists believed that
questions.e: Sequence convergence 'had been thought rare enough to serve as a reliable sign of shared ancestry,' so a shared genetic change was taken to indicate common descent rather than independent evolution. The passage calls convergence in form 'common,' the reverse of the third choice, and it never suggests that echolocation was thought to have a single origin.
o: echolocation had evolved only once among mammals, in an ancestor shared by bats and toothed whales
convergence in form between unrelated animals was too rare to be studied with statistical methods
identical genetic changes in two lineages more likely reflected common descent than independent evolution
genes involved in hearing were much less likely than other genes to change over evolutionary time
molecular comparisons could never reveal anything useful about the evolution of a complex behavior like echolocation

questions.s: The passage suggests which of the following about foreignizing translation? Select all that apply.
questions.e: Because 'What strikes one audience as foreign depends on that audience's habits,' the same foreignizing rendering may seem exotic at one time and ordinary at another. Foreignization is defined as preserving 'customs and allusions,' so the second statement contradicts the passage, and its advocates call it 'the more respectful, even the more ethical, choice,' which reverses the third.
o: Its effect on readers is not fixed but depends on the habits of a particular audience.
It is incapable of conveying the customs of the culture in which a text originated.
Its advocates have generally regarded it as less faithful to the source than domestication.

questions.s: The author mentions readers who "attribute the clumsiness to the original author" in order to
questions.e: Foreignization aims to avoid erasing the source, yet clumsy literalism can make readers misjudge the original author, 'a distortion no less serious than the one foreignization was meant to avoid.' The author complicates the dichotomy without declaring domestication 'always' more faithful, and the change in audience habits is a separate point made in the previous sentence.
o: argue that domesticating translations are always more faithful to the original author than foreignizing ones
suggest that most readers of translations cannot recognize idiomatic prose in their own language
illustrate how the expectations of an audience shift from one decade to the next over time
explain why advocates of foreignization regard their approach as the more ethical of the two
show that a strategy meant to prevent distortion can produce a distortion of its own

questions.s: Select the sentence that presents evidence about timing and location that a purely climatic explanation has difficulty accommodating.
questions.e: The third sentence gives the evidence: southern cities emptied before the driest intervals, while drier northern cities flourished during them. The next sentence, 'Such a pattern is awkward for a purely climatic account,' draws the conclusion but presents no evidence itself, and the first sentence offers sediment evidence that supports the drought account.
o: The abandonment of many lowland Maya cities in the ninth century has often been attributed to drought, and lake sediments from the region do record several severe dry periods at about that time.
Yet the decline did not unfold as a single event.
Some cities in the southern lowlands were emptied decades before the driest intervals, while others in the north, where rainfall was lower to begin with, flourished during them.
Such a pattern is awkward for a purely climatic account.
Many archaeologists now describe drought as a stress that acted on societies already strained by warfare among rival dynasties and by heavy demands on farmland.
On this view, the crucial question is not whether the climate changed but why some states could absorb the shock while others could not.
Answering it requires evidence of political organization that sediment cores cannot supply.

questions.s: The passage suggests that the view held by many archaeologists differs from the drought explanation chiefly in
questions.e: The archaeologists describe drought as 'a stress' acting on societies already strained by war and land use, and ask why some states 'could absorb the shock while others could not,' so climate becomes one factor whose impact varied. They accept the dry periods, they say political evidence is needed beyond sediment cores, and 'entirely to warfare' ignores the role they still give drought.
o: treating climate as one pressure among several whose effects depended on local conditions
denying that any severe dry periods occurred in the region at all during the ninth century
holding that the northern cities were abandoned well before the cities of the southern lowlands
relying on lake sediments rather than on evidence about the political organization of the region
attributing the decline of the cities entirely to warfare among the rival dynasties of the lowlands

questions.s: The primary purpose of the passage is to
questions.e: After presenting shuffling as a hoped-for adaptation, the author points to 'a trade-off that is easy to overlook' (less food, slower growth) and to evidence that the protection fades when temperatures normalize. Expulsion of algae is mentioned only as background, and the passage contrasts shuffling with 'slow genetic change,' so the claim that genetic change is faster reverses it.
o: explain in detail why rising water temperatures cause corals to expel the algae in their tissues
argue that genetic change in corals will proceed more rapidly than the shuffling of their algae
describe a new method that scientists have developed for transplanting heat-tolerant algae into corals
temper optimism about a proposed mechanism by pointing to its costs and limits
show that shuffling is unknown among corals that host more than one type of alga in their tissues

questions.s: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage about corals whose algal communities have shifted toward heat-tolerant types? Select all that apply.
questions.e: Heat-tolerant algae 'supply their hosts with less food,' and on monitored reefs the hardier algae were replaced by the original types 'once temperatures returned to normal.' The corals still host algae, merely of a different type, so they have not stopped depending on them.
o: They no longer depend on algae for their survival.
They may obtain less nourishment from their algae than before the shift.
They may lose their heat-tolerant algae if water temperatures fall back to normal.

questions.s: According to the passage, the shortening of exposure times is significant because
questions.e: Exposures had shrunk to 'a few seconds by the 1860s,' yet 'unsmiling faces remained the convention for decades afterward,' which shows that exposure time alone cannot explain the solemnity. It is the long exposures, not their shortening, that explain why early sitters could not hold a smile, and nothing says painters changed their views.
o: it allowed photographers for the first time to copy the poses and props of portrait painters
the convention it might have ended persisted long after it occurred
it led portrait painters to abandon the association of open smiles with foolishness
it made blurred images far more common in portraits taken during the 1860s than earlier
it explains why the sitters in the earliest photographs could not hold a smile for half a minute

questions.s: Select the sentence in which the author grants that an explanation is partly correct before qualifying it.
questions.e: The second sentence says 'The technical explanation is true as far as it goes, but' then notes that solemn faces outlasted long exposures. The last sentence also limits the role of technology, but it states the historians' conclusion rather than conceding and then qualifying an explanation.
o: Portraits from the first decades of photography show sitters who rarely smile, and the solemnity is often explained by the long exposures early processes required: a grin held for half a minute becomes a grimace, and a blurred one besides.
The technical explanation is true as far as it goes, but exposure times had shortened to a few seconds by the 1860s, and unsmiling faces remained the convention for decades afterward.
Some historians therefore look to older traditions of painted portraiture, in which an open smile was associated with drunkenness, foolishness or the stage.
A portrait was meant to record a person's settled character, not a passing mood, and the earliest photographers inherited this expectation along with many of the painters' poses and props.
On this view technology did not create the solemn photographic face; it merely failed, for a time, to challenge a convention that predated it.

questions.s: The tour guide's _____ knowledge of the city's history impressed the visitors, who kept asking her question after question.
questions.e: Visitors who are impressed and keep asking questions have found a guide who knows a great deal. Extensive and vast both mean very large in amount. Limited and scant are synonyms meaning small, which would hardly impress anyone. Personal could fit alone, since a guide might share her own memories, but it does not mean large in amount, and it has no partner.

questions.s: After weeks without rain, the farmers were _____ when the first heavy storm of the season finally arrived.
questions.e: Farmers who have waited weeks for rain would be very happy to see a storm. Delighted and overjoyed both mean very pleased. Dismayed and disappointed are synonyms that make no sense for rain the crops need. Surprised could fit alone, but "finally arrived" suggests the storm was awaited, and surprised has no partner.

questions.s: The children were so _____ during the long train ride that the other passengers barely noticed they were there.
questions.e: Passengers barely noticing the children shows they made little noise or fuss. Calm and peaceful both mean quiet and untroubled. Rowdy and unruly are synonyms meaning noisy and hard to control, which everyone would notice. Tired could explain quiet children, but it describes how they felt rather than how they behaved, and it has no partner.

questions.s: Sofia's explanation was so _____ that the whole class grasped the idea on the very first try.
questions.e: A class grasping an idea at once points to an explanation that was easy to follow. Understandable and comprehensible both mean that. Obscure and cryptic are synonyms meaning hard to understand, the opposite. Short could fit alone, but a short explanation is not necessarily clear, and no other choice means short.

questions.s: The company decided to _____ the product launch until all of the safety tests were complete.
questions.e: "Until all of the safety tests were complete" shows the launch was moved to a later date. Postpone and delay both mean that. Accelerate and hasten are synonyms meaning speed up, which cannot happen "until" the tests finish. Cancel fits the caution in the sentence, but cancelling means calling off for good, which clashes with "until," and cancel has no partner.

questions.s: The scientist's tone in the paper was _____; she presented her striking findings without a single boastful claim.
questions.e: Presenting striking findings without boasting describes a tone held in check. Restrained and understated both mean that. Grandiose and pompous are synonyms meaning self-important, the opposite of a tone with no boasting. Technical could describe a scientific paper, but it concerns vocabulary rather than modesty, and it has no partner.

questions.s: Although the new refund policy was meant to _____ confusion among customers, its wording only created more.
questions.e: "Although ... meant to" and "only created more" contrast the goal with the result, so the goal was less confusion. Lessen and diminish both mean make smaller. Compound and amplify are the trap: they describe what actually happened, not what was intended. Study could fit grammatically, but it does not contrast with creating more confusion, and it has no partner.

questions.s: Despite her _____ start as a clerk in a small shop, Amara went on to run one of the country's largest retailers.
questions.e: "Despite" contrasts the start with her later success, and a clerk in a small shop is a lowly beginning. Humble and modest both mean low in rank or size. Privileged and affluent are synonyms meaning wealthy, which would remove the contrast. Late could also contrast with great success, but it concerns timing rather than status, and it has no partner.

questions.s: The negotiator's offer was _____: it gave the other side nothing it had asked for while seeming to grant everything.
questions.e: An offer that seems to give everything but gives nothing creates a false impression. Deceptive and misleading both mean that. Generous and magnanimous are the trap: they describe how the offer seemed, not what it was. Final could fit alone, but it says nothing about the gap between appearance and substance, and it has no partner.

questions.s: Few observers expected the tiny startup to _____ its well-funded rivals, yet within five years it dominated the market.
questions.e: "Yet ... it dominated the market" shows the startup did surpass its rivals, which few expected. Eclipse and outstrip both mean surpass. Imitate and emulate are synonyms meaning copy, which does not match dominating the market. Challenge is tempting, but challenging rivals falls short of dominating them, and challenge has no partner.

questions.s: The diarist treats the great events of her day with surprising _____, recording a coronation in one flat sentence while devoting pages to her garden.
questions.e: One flat sentence for a coronation and pages for a garden show the great events left her unconcerned. Nonchalance and insouciance both mean casual lack of concern. Reverence and veneration are synonyms meaning deep respect, the opposite. Accuracy could fit alone, but the clue is about how much attention she gives, not whether she is correct; alacrity means eager readiness.

questions.s: Her colleagues dismissed her early warnings as _____, but the collapse she had predicted arrived on schedule.
questions.e: "Dismissed" and "but ... arrived on schedule" show the colleagues thought the warnings exaggerated. Alarmist (needlessly frightening) and overwrought (excessively emotional) both fit. Prescient and prophetic are the trap: they describe the warnings as they turned out, not how colleagues saw them. Unwelcome could fit alone, but people can find a warning unwelcome while still believing it, and it has no partner.

questions.s: The once _____ critic has mellowed with age, and her recent reviews find something to admire in nearly every book.
questions.e: "Once" and "has mellowed" contrast a harsh past with a kinder present. Mordant (bitingly sarcastic) and scathing (severely critical) both fit. Genial and affable are synonyms meaning friendly, which describe her now. Influential could fit alone, but it does not contrast with mellowing, and it has no partner.

questions.s: Though the mathematician's proof is _____, filling only a single page, it settled a question that had resisted far longer attacks for a century.
questions.e: "Filling only a single page" restates the blank, so the proof is brief. Compact and pithy (brief and full of meaning) both fit. Discursive and rambling are synonyms meaning wandering from topic to topic, the opposite. Elementary could fit alone, since a simple proof may surprise experts, but it means basic rather than short, and it has no partner.

questions.s: Far from being _____, the archive's catalog contains so many errors that scholars routinely find documents filed under the wrong century.
questions.e: "Far from being" means the catalog is the opposite of the blank, and it is full of errors, so the blank means free of mistakes. Infallible and unerring both mean never wrong. Slipshod and shoddy are the trap: they describe the catalog as it really is, which "far from" rules out. Accessible could fit grammatically, but ease of use does not contrast with error, and it has no partner.

questions.s: The guidebook's directions were so _____ that we reached the hidden waterfall without a single wrong turn.
questions.e: Reaching the waterfall "without a single wrong turn" shows that the directions were correct in every detail: accurate and exact. Misleading and deceptive are synonyms, but they would have caused wrong turns. Short directions could still be followed, yet length does not explain success, and short has no partner.

questions.s: Chen's _____ for chemistry was evident early: by the age of twelve he was running careful experiments in his family's garage.
questions.e: Running careful experiments at twelve shows a natural ability: aptitude and flair (a natural talent). Aversion and distaste are synonyms for dislike, which would not lead to experiments in the garage. Enthusiasm also fits, but eagerness is not the same as ability, so a sentence with enthusiasm would mean something different, and it has no partner.

questions.s: The old factory had been _____ for years, its windows broken and its machinery left to rust.
questions.e: Broken windows and rusting machinery show that nobody had used or cared for the building: abandoned and deserted. Renovated and restored are synonyms for repaired, which contradicts the description. Unheated fits an empty building, but it describes only the temperature, not the neglect, and unheated has no partner.

questions.s: The professor's comments on the essay were _____ but fair: she pointed out every weakness while still acknowledging its strengths.
questions.e: "But fair" concedes something negative about the comments, and pointing out "every weakness" explains it: harsh and severe. Lenient and gentle are synonyms, but a lenient reader would not point out every weakness, so they clash with the colon clause. Detailed fits a professor who notes every weakness, yet detail is not a fault to be offset by fairness, and detailed has no partner.

questions.s: Because the region's climate is so _____, farmers there can grow crops throughout the year.
questions.e: Growing crops all year requires a climate without harsh extremes, so the blank means mild or temperate. Frigid and icy are synonyms for very cold, which would stop crops from growing in winter. Wet fits farming, since crops need water, but rain alone does not allow a year-round season, and wet has no partner.

questions.s: The manager's _____ handling of the complaint, in which she apologized, offered a refund and fixed the problem within a day, won the customer's loyalty.
questions.e: Apologizing, refunding and fixing the problem quickly is skillful service, so the blank means adroit or deft (cleverly skillful). Clumsy and inept are synonyms for unskillful, which would not win loyalty. Public handling is possible, but doing something in public does not mean doing it well, and public has no partner.

questions.s: Far from _____ the reader, the essay's technical vocabulary is always defined in plain language the first time it appears.
questions.e: "Far from" sets the blank against clear definitions in plain language, so the vocabulary does not confuse the reader: confounding and perplexing. Engaging and captivating are synonyms, but clear definitions do not argue against interesting the reader, so the contrast fails. Insulting also fits grammatically, but jargon that offends is not the same as jargon that confuses, and plain definitions answer confusion, so insulting has no partner.

questions.s: The negotiations were _____, stretching over three years and several changes of leadership on both sides.
questions.e: Talks "stretching over three years" lasted a long time: protracted and drawn-out. Hasty and hurried are synonyms for rushed, the reverse of three years of talks. Secret negotiations can also last for years, but secrecy says nothing about length, and secret has no partner.

questions.s: Critics praised the actor's _____ performance, noting that he conveyed the character's grief through the smallest of gestures.
questions.e: Conveying grief "through the smallest of gestures" is restrained acting: understated and subtle. Histrionic and melodramatic are synonyms for exaggerated acting, and a hurried reader may link grief with big emotion, but the clue is small gestures. Brave could describe a praised performance, but it does not match the clue, and it has no partner. Arable describes land fit for crops.

questions.s: The town's water supply, long considered _____, was found last spring to contain traces of industrial chemicals.
questions.e: "Long considered" sets an old belief against the discovery of chemicals, so people thought the water was perfectly clean: pristine and uncontaminated. Polluted and tainted are synonyms describing what was actually found, so they remove the contrast. Plentiful fits a water supply, but quantity is not contradicted by contamination, and plentiful has no partner.

questions.s: The director's eventual _____ to the studio's demands surprised those who remembered her earlier refusal to change a single frame of her films.
questions.e: The surprise comes from a contrast with her earlier refusal to change anything, so this time she gave in: capitulation (surrender) and acquiescence (passive agreement). Defiance and recalcitrance (stubborn resistance) are synonyms that match her earlier behavior, so they would not surprise anyone. Reply is grammatical, but replying to demands is not a change from refusing, and reply has no partner. Perspicacity means keen insight.

questions.s: Far from being _____, the treatise's many digressions prove essential, each one anticipating an argument developed in later chapters.
questions.e: "Far from being" is set against "essential," so the blank means unnecessary: extraneous (not relevant) and gratuitous (uncalled for). Integral and indispensable are synonyms for essential, so they make the sentence contradict itself. Tedious is a fair complaint about digressions, but being boring is not the opposite of being essential, and tedious has no partner. Lambent means softly glowing.

questions.s: Although the critic's essays are dense with references to obscure texts, they never seem _____; her learning is worn lightly and always serves the argument.
questions.e: "Although" and "learning is worn lightly" deny the usual fault of heavy scholarship, which is a showy fussiness about learning: pedantic and donnish (bookish in a dry, academic way). Accessible and approachable are synonyms, but saying the essays "never seem accessible" contradicts "worn lightly." Dated could describe essays full of old references, but it is not what lightly worn learning avoids, and dated has no partner. Torpid means sluggish.

questions.s: The fossil record for the period is so _____ that paleontologists must reconstruct entire lineages from a handful of specimens.
questions.e: Having only "a handful of specimens" means very little evidence: exiguous (very small in amount) and scanty. Copious and abundant are synonyms for plentiful, which would make reconstruction from a handful unnecessary. Ancient is true of any fossil record, but age does not explain the shortage of specimens, and ancient has no partner. Fractious means unruly.

questions.s: The lecturer's _____ style, jumping from topic to topic with no apparent plan, left students struggling to take coherent notes.
questions.e: "Jumping from topic to topic with no apparent plan" defines a wandering style: rambling and digressive (straying from the main subject). Orderly and methodical are synonyms describing a planned lecture, the opposite of the clue. Rapid speech can also make note-taking hard, but speed is not the same as lack of plan, and rapid has no partner. Impecunious means having little money.

questions.s: Although the new manager was _____ in meetings, her written memos were long and full of detail.
questions.e: The contrast word "Although" and the phrase "long and full of detail" call for a word meaning brief in speech. Succinct and concise both mean expressing much in few words. Verbose and wordy are a synonym pair, but they describe the memos, not the contrasting meetings. Silent could fit on its own, but no other choice means silent, and saying nothing is not the same as speaking briefly.

questions.s: The museum guards were unusually _____ that day, checking every bag twice and watching each visitor who came near the paintings.
questions.e: Checking bags twice and watching each visitor describe people who pay close attention, so the blank means alert. Vigilant and watchful both mean keeping careful watch for danger or trouble. Careless and negligent are synonyms that say the opposite. Strict could fit alone, but it is about enforcing rules rather than watching closely, and it has no partner among the choices.

questions.s: Reviewers praised the novel for its _____ portrait of farm life, noting that every detail of the daily routine rang true.
questions.e: The clue "every detail ... rang true" calls for a word meaning true to life. Realistic and lifelike both say the portrait matches reality. Fanciful and whimsical form a synonym pair, but imaginative and playful is the opposite of what the clue describes. Affectionate could describe a portrait on its own, yet nothing else means affectionate, and warmth is not accuracy.

questions.s: Because the old bridge had been _____ for decades, engineers were not surprised when inspectors found deep cracks in its supports.
questions.e: Cracks that surprise no one suggest the bridge was not cared for, so the blank means left without attention. Neglected and disregarded both say that. Renovated and restored are synonyms, but repair work would make the cracks surprising, not expected. Overloaded also explains cracks, but it names a different cause and has no partner.

questions.s: The new menu was so _____ that diners who had ordered the same dish every week for years began trying something different.
questions.e: Long-time regulars changing their order shows the menu drew them in, so the blank means attractive. Enticing and tempting both mean arousing a desire to try something. Bland and dull are synonyms that would keep diners with their old dish. Inexpensive could also explain the change, but no other choice means cheap, so it cannot form a pair.

questions.s: Despite the team's _____ start to the season, when it lost its first six games, it finished the year in first place.
questions.e: "Despite" sets the start against a first-place finish, and losing six games shows the start was very bad. Dismal and miserable both mean very poor. Brilliant and stellar are a synonym pair, but they contradict the six losses. Unexpected could fit alone, since a bad start may surprise fans, but nothing else means unexpected.

questions.s: The speaker's _____ remarks put the nervous audience at ease, and soon the whole room was laughing.
questions.e: Laughter in the room shows the remarks were funny. Witty and amusing both describe remarks that make people laugh. Solemn and grave are synonyms meaning serious, the opposite of what the laughter shows. Friendly could put people at ease, but it does not explain the laughing and has no partner.

questions.s: The witness's account was so _____ that the jury could not work out what had actually happened on the night in question.
questions.e: A jury unable to work out events points to an account that was hard to follow. Confusing and incoherent both describe speech that does not make sense as a whole. Lucid and clear are synonyms but say the reverse. Brief could also leave the jury unsure, yet it means short rather than hard to follow, and no other word means brief.

questions.s: Many early inventors were _____ by repeated failures; instead of quitting, they treated each setback as a lesson.
questions.e: "Instead of quitting" shows the failures did not stop them. Undeterred and undaunted both mean not put off by difficulty. Discouraged and disheartened are a tempting synonym pair, but they contradict the refusal to quit. Educated fits the idea of lessons, but it has no partner and says nothing about whether they gave up.

questions.s: The mountain village is so _____ that the nearest shop is a two-hour drive along a single narrow road.
questions.e: A shop two hours away describes a place far from others. Remote and isolated both mean far from other places. Crowded and bustling are synonyms describing busy places, which the clue does not support. Small could fit alone, but a small village is not necessarily far from shops, and nothing else means small.

questions.s: Rather than _____ the error, the company announced it publicly and explained how it would fix the problem.
questions.e: "Rather than" contrasts the blank with announcing the error, so the blank means keep it secret. Conceal and hide both mean that. Acknowledge and confess are a synonym pair, but they repeat what the company did instead of contrasting with it. Deny fits the contrast too, but denying means claiming the error did not happen, which is different from hiding it, and deny has no partner.

questions.s: The chemist's results proved _____: three other laboratories repeated the experiment and obtained the same findings.
questions.e: The colon introduces support: other labs got the same findings, so the results can be trusted. Reliable and dependable both mean consistently trustworthy. Dubious and questionable are synonyms that say the opposite. Surprising might describe new results, but repeated confirmation shows trustworthiness, not surprise, and nothing pairs with surprising.

questions.s: Although the hiking trail looked _____ on the map, it turned out to be steep, rocky and exhausting.
questions.e: "Although" sets the map's impression against a steep, exhausting trail, so the blank means not difficult. Easy and effortless both fit. Arduous and grueling are synonyms meaning very hard, which removes the contrast. Short could fit alone, since a short trail can still be steep, but no other choice means short.

questions.s: The two sisters had _____ tastes in music: one loved loud rock bands, while the other listened only to quiet piano pieces.
questions.e: Loud rock against quiet piano shows the sisters' tastes differ. Dissimilar and contrasting both say that. Identical and matching are a synonym pair, but the examples show the reverse. Unusual could describe someone's taste, yet the sentence is about how the two tastes compare, and unusual has no partner.

questions.s: The mayor's plan was popular at first, but public support _____ once residents learned how much it would cost.
questions.e: "But" contrasts with early popularity, and cost news usually lowers support, so the blank means became smaller. Faded and dwindled both mean gradually shrank. Grew and increased are synonyms that remove the contrast. Split could fit alone, since a cost might divide residents, but no other choice means divided.

questions.s: The assembly instructions were so _____ that even first-time buyers put the bookshelf together in a few minutes.
questions.e: Quick assembly by beginners shows the instructions were easy to follow. Straightforward and uncomplicated both mean simple and easy to understand. Convoluted and intricate are a synonym pair meaning complex, which would slow beginners down. Illustrated could explain the quick assembly, but no other choice means having pictures.

questions.s: The young pianist's debut was _____: critics who had expected a nervous beginner heard instead a confident and polished artist.
questions.e: The colon explains the blank: critics expected a nervous beginner but found a polished artist, so the debut stood out. Impressive and remarkable both mean worthy of notice and praise. Mediocre and ordinary are synonyms that contradict the critics' surprise. Emotional could describe a performance, but it has no partner and does not capture the confidence and polish.

questions.s: Kwame was _____ about his chances of winning the scholarship, so he also applied to several other programs as a backup.
questions.e: Applying elsewhere as a backup suggests Kwame did not expect to win. Pessimistic and gloomy both mean expecting a bad outcome. Optimistic and hopeful are synonyms that point the other way. Realistic could fit alone, since a sensible person makes backup plans, but it means judging accurately rather than expecting the worst, and it has no partner.

questions.s: The factory's new machines are far more _____ than the old ones, making twice as many parts with the same amount of electricity.
questions.e: More output from the same energy describes machines that make good use of resources. Efficient and economical both mean using resources without waste. Wasteful and extravagant are a synonym pair with the opposite meaning. Expensive could be true of new machines, but the clue is about output per unit of electricity, and expensive has no partner.

questions.s: Mateo's apology seemed _____; he smiled throughout and repeated the same insult a few minutes later.
questions.e: Repeating the insult soon after shows Mateo did not mean his apology. Insincere and hollow both describe words without real feeling behind them. Heartfelt and earnest are synonyms meaning sincere, the opposite. Rehearsed could fit on its own, but a practiced apology is not necessarily false, and no other choice means rehearsed.

questions.s: Unlike her _____ older brother, who rarely spoke to strangers, Sofia chatted easily with everyone she met.
questions.e: The brother "rarely spoke to strangers," in contrast to Sofia's easy chatting, so he is timid with people. Shy and bashful both mean that. Outgoing and sociable are synonyms that describe Sofia, not her brother. Cautious could fit alone, but it means careful about risk rather than timid with people, and it has no partner.

questions.s: The heavy rain made the dirt road nearly _____, so the delivery truck had to take a much longer route.
questions.e: A truck forced onto a longer route could not travel the road, so the blank means not able to be used for travel. Impassable and unusable both say that. Smooth and level are synonyms describing an easy road, which would not force a detour. Invisible could explain a detour in heavy rain, but no other choice means unseen.

questions.s: Scientists remain _____ about the cause of the decline in bee populations, and several competing explanations are still being tested.
questions.e: Competing explanations still under test show that no answer has been settled. Uncertain and undecided both mean not yet sure. Adamant and insistent are a synonym pair meaning firmly committed to a view, the opposite. Curious could fit alone, since scientists want to know the cause, but it does not say whether they have an answer, and it has no partner.

questions.s: The documentary offered a _____ account of the ship's construction, covering everything from the first design sketches to the final coat of paint.
questions.e: "Covering everything" restates the blank, so it means complete. Thorough and comprehensive both describe an account that leaves nothing out. Sketchy and superficial are synonyms meaning lacking detail, the reverse. Dramatic could describe a documentary, but it is about style rather than completeness, and no other word means dramatic.

questions.s: The library's rules are _____: anyone who returns a book late, even by a single day, must pay a fine.
questions.e: A fine for being one day late shows that the rules allow no exceptions. Strict and rigid both mean firmly enforced. Lax and lenient are a synonym pair meaning loose or forgiving, the opposite. Fair could fit on its own, since the rule applies to everyone, but it is a judgment about justice rather than firmness, and it has no partner.

questions.s: Visitors often find the city's subway map _____ at first, but after a few rides they learn to navigate it without trouble.
questions.e: "But after a few rides they learn" shows the map is hard to understand at first. Perplexing and mystifying both mean very confusing. Obvious and evident are synonyms meaning easy to see, which removes the contrast with learning over time. Colorful could describe a map, but it has no partner and does not set up the contrast.

questions.s: The teacher's _____ praise encouraged the shy student to share her poems with the rest of the class.
questions.e: Praise that encourages a shy student to share is sincere and enthusiastic. Hearty and warm both describe praise given with real feeling. Grudging and reluctant are synonyms meaning given unwillingly, which would hardly encourage her. Private could fit alone, since quiet praise might help a shy student, but no other choice means private.

questions.s: The ancient manuscript is extremely _____, so researchers may handle it only while wearing gloves and only for a few minutes at a time.
questions.e: Gloves and very short handling times protect something easily damaged. Fragile and delicate both mean easily broken or harmed. Sturdy and durable are a synonym pair meaning strong, which would not need such care. Valuable also explains careful handling, but it means worth a lot rather than easily damaged, and it has no partner.

questions.s: The company's profits have been _____ this year, rising sharply in one quarter and falling just as sharply in the next.
questions.e: Sharp rises followed by sharp falls describe irregular change. Erratic and unpredictable both mean changing without a regular pattern. Steady and constant are synonyms that contradict the ups and downs. Disappointing could fit alone, but the clue describes the pattern of change, not whether it was good or bad, and nothing pairs with disappointing.

questions.s: The guest lecture was so _____ that several students fell asleep before the speaker reached the halfway point.
questions.e: Students falling asleep points to a lecture that failed to hold attention. Tedious and boring both mean dull and tiresome. Riveting and gripping are a synonym pair meaning very interesting, the opposite. Early could fit on its own, since tired students might doze at an early hour, but no other choice means early.

questions.s: Though the essay was praised on publication as _____, a close reading shows that it merely restates arguments made decades earlier.
questions.e: "Though" sets the praise against the finding that the essay only restates old arguments, so the praise must have been for originality. Innovative and trailblazing both mean introducing new ideas. Derivative and unoriginal are synonyms, but they describe what the close reading found, not the praise it overturns. Eloquent could be praise, yet restating old ideas does not contradict eloquence, and it has no partner.

questions.s: Far from being _____, the evidence for the newly reported species rests on a single blurred photograph taken at dusk.
questions.e: "Far from being" means the evidence is the opposite of the blank, and one blurred photograph is weak evidence, so the blank means settling the question. Conclusive and definitive both mean that. Tenuous and flimsy are the trap: they do describe the evidence, but "far from being" reverses them. Recent could fit grammatically, but nothing pairs with it and it ignores the contrast.

questions.s: Amara's _____ manner in negotiations often misled her opponents, who mistook her calm courtesy for a lack of resolve.
questions.e: "Calm courtesy" restates the blank, so it means calm and untroubled. Placid and serene both mean that. Volatile and temperamental are synonyms meaning prone to sudden moods, the reverse of calm. Deliberate could describe a negotiator, but it means slow and intentional, does not explain the misreading as weakness, and has no partner.

questions.s: The historian argued that the empire's collapse was not sudden but _____, the result of slow decay spread over several centuries.
questions.e: "Not sudden but" and "slow decay" call for a word meaning step by step. Gradual and incremental both mean happening in small stages over time. Abrupt and precipitous are synonyms meaning sudden, which the sentence denies. Inevitable fits the historian's view in general, but it means bound to happen rather than slow, and nothing else means inevitable.

questions.s: Seasoned investors dismissed the startup's projections as _____, since they assumed that sales would triple every year for a decade.
questions.e: Tripling sales every year for ten years is hard to believe, and "dismissed" shows the investors did not believe it. Implausible and far-fetched both mean unlikely to be true. Conservative and cautious are a synonym pair, but they describe modest forecasts, the opposite of these. Ambitious does describe the projections, but calling a plan ambitious is not a reason to dismiss it as unbelievable, and ambitious has no partner.

questions.s: Although the film's plot is _____, its striking photography kept audiences in their seats until the final scene.
questions.e: "Although" sets the plot against the photography that held audiences, so the plot is a weakness. Trite and hackneyed both mean overused and unoriginal. Inventive and imaginative are synonyms that would make the plot a strength and remove the contrast. Confusing could also be a weakness, but nothing else means confusing, so it cannot form a pair.

questions.s: The committee's report was deliberately _____, avoiding any firm conclusion so that no member would have grounds to object.
questions.e: Avoiding any firm conclusion on purpose describes language that does not take a position. Equivocal (open to more than one interpretation, often to avoid commitment) and noncommittal both mean that. Candid and forthright are synonyms meaning frank and direct, the opposite. Diplomatic is close but means tactful, which a report can be while still reaching a firm conclusion, and it has no partner.

questions.s: Chen's early paintings were _____ by critics during his lifetime, yet after his death the same works sold for record prices.
questions.e: "Yet" sets the critics' response against later record prices, so the critics thought little of the works. Disparaged and belittled both mean spoken of as having little value. Acclaimed and lauded are synonyms meaning praised, which removes the contrast. Ignored also contrasts with later success, but being ignored is different from being criticized, and ignored has no partner.

questions.s: The regulation was intended to _____ air pollution in the valley, but in its first year emissions actually rose.
questions.e: "But ... emissions actually rose" shows the intent was the opposite: to lower pollution. Curb and reduce both mean that. Exacerbate (make worse) and worsen are synonyms, but no rule is intended to raise pollution, and they kill the contrast. Measure could fit alone, but measuring pollution does not conflict with rising emissions, and it has no partner.

questions.s: Olga's reputation for _____ was well earned: she checked every figure in the annual report three times before submitting it.
questions.e: Checking every figure three times is the evidence after the colon, so the blank means great care with detail. Thoroughness and meticulousness (extreme attention to detail) both fit. Negligence and carelessness are a synonym pair with the opposite meaning. Honesty is a virtue an accountant might have, but rechecking figures shows care rather than honesty, and nothing pairs with it.

questions.s: The once _____ fishing town has grown quiet since the cannery closed, and many of its shops now stand empty.
questions.e: "Once" signals a contrast with the town's present state, quiet with empty shops, so the blank means doing well. Thriving and prosperous both mean flourishing economically. Sleepy and drowsy are the trap: they describe the town now, not as it once was. Crowded also contrasts with the present, but it is about numbers of people rather than economic health, and it has no partner.

questions.s: The author's prose is notably _____; she uses few adjectives and seldom writes a sentence longer than ten words.
questions.e: Few adjectives and short sentences describe plain, stripped-down writing. Unadorned and stark (bare, without decoration) both mean that. Florid and ornate are synonyms meaning heavily decorated, the opposite. Precise could fit alone, but exact wording can still be long and rich, and no other choice means precise.

questions.s: Far from _____ the dispute, the mediator's clumsy remarks only made both sides angrier than before.
questions.e: "Far from" means the remarks did the opposite of the blank, and they made both sides angrier, so the blank means easing the conflict. Defusing and calming both do. Inflaming and aggravating are the trap: they describe what actually happened, which "far from" rules out. Understanding could fit, but it has no partner and does not contrast with making people angry.

questions.s: The theory was at first dismissed as _____, but later experiments confirmed nearly all of its predictions.
questions.e: "Dismissed" and "but later ... confirmed" show the theory was first thought absurd. Outlandish (bizarre) and preposterous (absurd) both fit. Sound and valid are synonyms, but no one dismisses a theory for being sound, and they erase the contrast. Premature could fit alone, since a theory can be ahead of its evidence, but it has no partner.

questions.s: Though the trade agreement was hailed as a lasting settlement, it proved _____, collapsing within two years of its signing.
questions.e: "Though ... lasting" and "collapsing within two years" call for a word meaning brief in duration. Ephemeral (lasting a very short time) and short-lived both mean that. Enduring and permanent are synonyms that repeat the hope the sentence contradicts. Costly could fit alone, but it does not match the collapse after two years, and nothing pairs with it.

questions.s: Priya's _____ remarks about the proposal, delivered without any of her usual tact, surprised colleagues who were used to her diplomacy.
questions.e: "Without any of her usual tact" restates the blank, so it means abrupt and plain-spoken. Blunt and brusque (abrupt to the point of rudeness) both fit. Tactful and diplomatic are synonyms describing her usual manner, the very thing these remarks lacked. Critical could fit alone, but criticism can be delivered tactfully, and no other choice means critical.

questions.s: The wildcat is so _____ in the region that hikers almost never see one, even on trails that cross the middle of its range.
questions.e: Hikers almost never seeing the animal, even within its range, suggests there are few of them. Scarce and rare both mean present in small numbers. Ubiquitous (found everywhere) and pervasive are synonyms with the opposite sense. Nocturnal also explains why hikers miss the animal, but it means active at night rather than few in number, and it has no partner.

questions.s: Despite their _____ public statements about each other, the two companies had been quietly cooperating on research for years.
questions.e: "Despite" sets the public statements against quiet cooperation, so the statements were unfriendly. Antagonistic and hostile both mean openly opposed. Cordial and amicable are synonyms meaning friendly, which removes the contrast. Infrequent could fit grammatically, but rare statements do not conflict with cooperation, and nothing pairs with it.

questions.s: The coach's strategy, though _____ at first glance, had been carefully designed to tire out the opposing team's best players.
questions.e: "Though ... at first glance" contrasts appearance with the careful design, so the strategy looked unplanned. Haphazard and random both mean lacking any plan. Calculated and deliberate are the trap: they describe what the strategy really was, not how it looked. Risky could fit alone, but it does not contrast with careful design, and it has no partner.

questions.s: Because the data set was so _____, the researchers could draw only tentative conclusions about the disease's spread.
questions.e: Only tentative conclusions follow from too little data, so the blank means small in amount. Sparse and meager both mean scanty. Abundant and copious are synonyms meaning plentiful, which would support firmer conclusions. Outdated could also weaken conclusions, but it is about age rather than amount, and no other choice means outdated.

questions.s: The director is famously _____, rarely granting interviews and declining to discuss the meaning of her films in public.
questions.e: Rarely giving interviews and refusing to explain her work describe someone who keeps her thoughts to herself. Reticent (not revealing one's thoughts readily) and guarded both mean that. Garrulous and loquacious are synonyms meaning very talkative, the opposite. Modest could fit alone, since a modest person may avoid attention, but it means humble rather than reserved, and it has no partner.

questions.s: What began as a _____ disagreement over office supplies eventually grew into a feud that divided the entire department.
questions.e: "Began as" and "eventually grew into a feud" contrast a small start with a large result, and office supplies are a minor matter. Trivial and petty both mean of little importance. Momentous and weighty are synonyms meaning very important, which removes the contrast. Polite could also contrast with a feud, but it describes manners rather than importance, and nothing pairs with it.

questions.s: Although the architect's facades look _____, each one follows strict mathematical rules about proportion and spacing.
questions.e: "Although" sets appearance against strict rules, so the facades look as if no rule governs them. Unplanned and unstructured both fit. Methodical and systematic are the trap: they describe how the facades are actually built. Futuristic could fit alone, but modern-looking buildings do not contradict mathematical rules, and it has no partner.

questions.s: The economist's forecast was _____: she predicted a modest slowdown, neither the collapse her rivals feared nor the boom they hoped for.
questions.e: The colon explains the blank: a modest slowdown, avoiding both extremes, is a middle-of-the-road prediction. Measured and moderate both mean restrained and not extreme. Extreme and radical are synonyms that describe the rivals' views, not hers. Accurate could fit alone, but the sentence never says whether the forecast came true, and no other choice means accurate.

questions.s: In contrast to his _____ predecessor, who announced every decision with great ceremony, the new director made his changes quietly.
questions.e: The predecessor announced every decision with great ceremony, the opposite of quiet change, so the blank means fond of display. Flamboyant and showy both mean that. Unassuming and self-effacing are synonyms meaning modest and retiring, which describe the new director instead. Popular could fit grammatically, but it does not match the clue about ceremony, and it has no partner.

questions.s: The quality of the restaurant's food has been _____ since the new owners arrived: excellent one night and barely edible the next.
questions.e: Excellent one night and barely edible the next describes quality that varies. Inconsistent and uneven both mean not the same from one time to the next. Impeccable and flawless are synonyms that contradict the barely edible nights. Declining is tempting because the change began with new owners, but the clue shows swings rather than a steady fall, and declining has no partner.

questions.s: Scholars once regarded the poet as a minor figure, but recent studies have done much to _____ her reputation.
questions.e: "Once ... minor figure, but recent studies" signals a change for the better. Enhance and elevate both mean raise or improve. Tarnish and sully are synonyms meaning damage, which would continue the old view rather than contrast with it. Examine could fit grammatically, but it does not show the change the contrast requires, and nothing pairs with it.

questions.s: Because the written instructions were _____, the volunteers interpreted them in at least three different ways.
questions.e: Three different interpretations show the instructions could be read more than one way. Ambiguous and unclear both fit. Explicit and unequivocal (leaving no doubt) are synonyms meaning the reverse. Lengthy could fit alone, but long instructions can still be clear, and no other choice means long.

questions.s: The founder was _____ in her search for investors, calling dozens of firms a week even after repeated rejections.
questions.e: Calling dozens of firms a week despite rejections shows unflagging effort. Persistent and indefatigable (incapable of being tired out) both mean continuing without giving up. Halfhearted and lukewarm are synonyms meaning lacking enthusiasm, the opposite. Desperate could also explain the many calls, but it names a feeling of hopelessness rather than persistence, and it has no partner.

questions.s: Her account of the expedition is admirably _____, crediting the porters and guides whose contributions earlier writers had ignored.
questions.e: Giving credit to people earlier writers ignored shows fairness to everyone involved, and "admirably" marks this as praise. Balanced and evenhanded both mean fair to all sides. Partisan and biased are synonyms meaning one-sided, which describes the earlier writers instead. Vivid could be praise for a travel account, but it concerns style rather than fairness, and nothing pairs with it.

questions.s: The columnist's endorsement of the novel was so _____ that readers finished her review unsure whether she had liked the book at all.
questions.e: An endorsement that leaves readers unsure of the columnist's opinion must be heavily limited. Hedged and qualified both describe statements weakened by reservations. Effusive and fulsome (lavish, even excessive) are a synonym pair, but unrestrained praise would leave no doubt. Terse could fit, since a very short endorsement may be hard to read, but brevity is not the same as reservation, and terse has no partner; pellucid (very clear) contradicts the reader's confusion.

questions.s: Though often portrayed as a _____, the mathematician in fact corresponded with dozens of colleagues and hosted a weekly seminar in her home.
questions.e: "In fact" corrects the portrayal with evidence of a busy social and intellectual life, so she was portrayed as someone who avoids others. Recluse and hermit both mean that. Sycophant and toady (a person who flatters the powerful) are synonyms, but the correction says nothing about flattery. Genius could fit alone, since mathematicians are often portrayed that way, but corresponding with colleagues does not contradict genius, and it has no partner.

questions.s: Initially _____ about the merger, the board grew enthusiastic once an outside auditor confirmed the projected savings.
questions.e: "Initially" and "grew enthusiastic once ... confirmed" mark a change from suspicion to support. Leery and wary both mean cautious and distrustful. Sanguine (cheerfully confident) and optimistic are synonyms that leave no change for the sentence to describe. Uninformed could fit alone, since the audit supplied information, but it describes knowledge rather than attitude, and nothing pairs with it.

questions.s: The physicist was _____ in her refusal to publish until every result had been replicated, even when rivals threatened to announce the discovery first.
questions.e: Holding firm even under the threat of being beaten to the discovery shows she would not budge. Intransigent and obdurate both mean stubbornly refusing to change one's position. Vacillating and irresolute are synonyms meaning wavering, the opposite. Scrupulous (careful about doing what is right) is the trap: it suits a scientist who insists on replication, but it does not mean unbending, and it has no partner.

questions.s: The athlete's _____ manner, which reduced every answer to a single word, made the interview an ordeal for the young reporter.
questions.e: Answers of a single word describe someone who says very little. Laconic (using very few words) and taciturn (habitually silent) both fit. Voluble (talking readily and at length) and prolix (tediously long-winded) are close in meaning but say the opposite. Hostile could also make an interview an ordeal, but one-word answers show brevity rather than anger, and hostile has no partner.

questions.s: The essay's argument is so _____ that summarizing it requires first untangling several interlocking digressions.
questions.e: An argument that must be untangled from interlocking digressions is intricate and hard to follow. Labyrinthine (like a maze) and tortuous (full of twists) both mean that. Pellucid and limpid are synonyms meaning transparently clear, the opposite. Provocative could fit alone, but a provocative argument can be easy to summarize, and no other choice pairs with it.

questions.s: The reviewer found the biography _____, faulting its author for reciting dates and appointments without ever conveying what made her subject remarkable.
questions.e: "Faulting" marks a negative verdict, and reciting dates without conveying what was remarkable describes flat, lifeless writing. Humdrum and mundane both mean dull and ordinary. Luminous and incandescent are synonyms meaning brilliant, which no one would offer as a fault. Exhaustive is the tempting single word, since a list of every date and appointment is thorough, but thoroughness is not dullness, and exhaustive has no partner; litigious means fond of lawsuits.

questions.s: The company's founder, once celebrated as a visionary, is now more often described as _____, having staked the firm's future on a series of impractical schemes.
questions.e: Betting everything on impractical schemes recasts vision as idealism that ignores reality. Quixotic (idealistic to an impractical degree) and unrealistic both mean that. Pragmatic and hardheaded are synonyms meaning practical and realistic, the opposite. Reckless is tempting, since staking a firm on risky plans is careless, but it does not capture the impractical idealism that turns a visionary into a dreamer, and it has no partner.

questions.s: The orchestra's new conductor is notably _____, rehearsing a single passage dozens of times until every note meets her standard.
questions.e: Rehearsing a passage dozens of times until every note is right describes someone who insists on precision. Exacting (making high demands) and punctilious (scrupulously attentive to detail) both fit. Slapdash and sloppy are synonyms meaning careless, the opposite. Patient could fit alone, since repetition takes patience, but patience does not imply high standards, and nothing pairs with it; diffident (lacking self-confidence) does not fit.

questions.s: The professor's lectures, though dense, are never _____; she enlivens even the most technical material with stories from her fieldwork.
questions.e: Enlivening material with stories prevents it from being dull, so the lectures are never lifeless. Arid (lacking interest) and dry both mean that. Abstruse and recondite (both meaning hard to understand) are the trap: they echo "dense" and "technical," but the sentence says "though dense," so difficulty is granted, not denied. Rushed could fit alone, but stories do not cure haste, and rushed has no partner.

questions.s: Previously thought to be _____, the disease is now known to spread only through contaminated water, never from one person to another.
questions.e: The new knowledge, "never from one person to another," corrects an old belief that it did spread between people. Contagious and communicable both mean transmissible from person to person. Benign and harmless are synonyms, but the correction concerns how the disease spreads, not its severity. Incurable could fit alone, but the new finding says nothing about cures, and incurable has no partner.

questions.s: Unlike her _____ colleagues, who readily adjusted their conclusions to please the funders, the economist refused to alter a single figure.
questions.e: The colleagues changed their findings to please the people paying them, so they were eager to please those in power. Obsequious and servile both mean excessively eager to please or obey. Obstinate and headstrong are synonyms meaning stubborn, which describes the economist rather than her colleagues. Underpaid could fit grammatically and might explain their behavior, but it has no partner.

questions.s: The novelist's later books, written after she achieved fame, are markedly more _____: the spare style of her early stories gives way to long, ornately decorated sentences.
questions.e: The colon explains the change: spare early style gives way to ornate sentences, so the later books are highly decorated. Baroque (extravagantly ornate) and embellished both mean that. Laconic and terse are synonyms that describe the early, spare style instead. Commercial could fit alone, since fame may push a writer toward sales, but the clue is about style, and commercial has no partner.

questions.s: The witness's testimony was riddled with _____, contradicting itself on the time, the place and even the people present.
questions.e: "Contradicting itself" restates the blank, so the testimony was full of parts that do not agree. Inconsistencies and discrepancies both mean that. Platitudes and banalities are synonyms meaning stale remarks, which have nothing to do with contradiction. Falsehoods is the tempting single word, but a statement can be false without contradicting itself, and falsehoods has no partner.

questions.s: Though the treatise's prose is _____, its argument rewards the patient reader with insights found nowhere else.
questions.e: "Though" and "the patient reader" suggest the prose is a barrier to be overcome. Forbidding (off-putting, discouraging approach) and inaccessible (hard to enter into or understand) both describe prose that resists the reader. Felicitous (well chosen and apt) and graceful are synonyms that remove the contrast. Repetitive could also try a reader's patience, but it means saying the same thing again rather than being hard to get into, and it has no partner; salubrious means healthful.

questions.s: The board hoped the new chief executive would be a _____ presence after years of turmoil, and she has indeed calmed the company's fractious divisions.
questions.e: "Indeed calmed" confirms the board's hope, so the blank means bringing calm and order. Stabilizing and steadying both mean that. Galvanizing and electrifying are synonyms meaning rousing people to action, which is not the same as calming fractious (quarrelsome) groups. Visible could fit alone, since a board may want an accessible leader, but it has no partner; truculent means eager to fight.

questions.s: Critics accused the historian of _____, noting that she quoted only the letters that supported her thesis and ignored dozens that did not.
questions.e: Quoting only supporting evidence and ignoring the rest is a charge of favoring one view. Partiality and one-sidedness both mean that. Plagiarism and piracy form a synonym pair about copying others' work, which the evidence does not mention. Laziness could fit alone, since ignoring dozens of letters might save effort, but the pattern of keeping only supporting letters points to bias, and laziness has no partner.

questions.s: Her _____ account of the negotiations, which omitted nothing and assigned an exact time to every exchange, became the standard reference for later historians.
questions.e: An account that "omitted nothing" and timed every exchange is complete in its detail. Exhaustive and detailed both mean that. Cursory and perfunctory are synonyms meaning hasty and superficial, the opposite. Firsthand is the tempting single word: it could explain why historians trusted the account, but it means from direct experience rather than complete, and it has no partner.

questions.s: The once _____ debating society has grown cautious, its members now preferring safe topics to the provocative motions that made it famous.
questions.e: "Once" and "has grown cautious" contrast past and present, and the provocative motions show the society used to take risks. Audacious and daring both mean boldly willing to take risks. Timid and fainthearted are the trap: they describe the society now, not as it once was. Prestigious also fits "made it famous," but it means respected rather than bold, and it has no partner.

questions.s: The biographer portrays her subject as thoroughly _____, a man so convinced of his own rightness that he never once admitted an error.
questions.e: Being so sure of one's own rightness that one never admits error describes someone who holds views as unquestionable. Dogmatic and opinionated both mean that. Diffident (lacking self-confidence) and unassertive are synonyms meaning the opposite. Solitary could fit grammatically, but it means living alone and has no partner; sartorial relates to clothing.

questions.s: The researcher's _____ approach, testing every possible combination of compounds rather than guessing which might work, took years but left nothing to chance.
questions.e: Testing every combination over years describes careful, effortful work. Laborious and painstaking both mean requiring great effort and care. Intuitive and instinctive are the trap: they describe the guessing the researcher rejected. Unorthodox could fit alone, but exhaustive testing is not necessarily unconventional, and it has no partner; lachrymose means tearful.

questions.s: The ostensibly _____ remark was in fact carefully calculated to embarrass her rival in front of the hiring panel.
questions.e: "Ostensibly" (apparently, on the surface) and "in fact carefully calculated" contrast how the remark looked with what it was, so it looked unplanned. Offhand and casual both mean that. Premeditated and intentional are the trap: they describe what the remark really was. Complimentary could also contrast with a hidden aim to embarrass, but it concerns praise rather than planning, and it has no partner.

questions.s: Although the region's climate is _____ for most of the year, sudden summer storms can drop a month's rain in a single afternoon.
questions.e: "Although" sets the usual climate against sudden violent storms, so the usual climate is mild and steady. Clement (mild, of weather) and equable (free from extremes) both fit. Inclement and stormy are synonyms that remove the contrast. Humid could fit alone, but humidity does not contrast with storms, and nothing pairs with it; pecuniary relates to money.

questions.s: The author has a gift for the _____ detail: a single well-chosen fact that illuminates an entire era.
questions.e: The colon defines the detail as one fact that illuminates a whole era, so it shows something important. Telling (strikingly revealing) and revealing both mean that. Extraneous and superfluous are synonyms meaning unnecessary, the opposite of a well-chosen fact. Obscure could fit alone, since a little-known fact can illuminate, but it means little known rather than revealing, and it has no partner.

questions.s: Long dismissed as a mere _____, the amateur astronomer turned out to have kept the most accurate observations of the comet ever recorded.
questions.e: "Dismissed as a mere" and "amateur" suggest someone thought not serious about the field. Dilettante and dabbler both mean a person who takes up a subject casually. Virtuoso and maestro are synonyms meaning a master, which no one would dismiss. Eccentric could fit alone, since odd people are often dismissed, but it concerns oddness rather than seriousness, and it has no partner.

questions.s: Despite the _____ of its opening chapters, which plod through family genealogy for nearly a hundred pages, the novel eventually becomes gripping.
questions.e: Chapters that "plod" for a hundred pages are dull, and "despite" sets them against the later gripping story. Tedium and monotony both mean tiresome sameness. Brevity and concision are synonyms meaning shortness, which a hundred plodding pages contradict. Obscurity could fit alone, since genealogy can be hard to follow, but it means unclearness rather than dullness, and it has no partner; levity means lightness of tone.

questions.s: Her reputation for _____ made her the obvious choice to mediate, since neither side doubted that she would weigh their claims fairly.
questions.e: Weighing claims fairly calls for freedom from bias. Impartiality and disinterestedness both mean that; disinterested means unbiased, not uninterested. Apathy and indifference are the trap for readers who confuse the two: lack of interest would make her a poor mediator. Patience is useful in a mediator and fits alone, but it does not explain trust in her fairness, and it has no partner.

questions.s: The theory's critics charge that it is _____: because it can accommodate any possible outcome, no experiment could ever show it to be wrong.
questions.e: The colon explains the charge: a theory that no experiment could ever refute cannot be put to the test. Unfalsifiable and untestable both mean that. Elegant and parsimonious (using few assumptions) both praise simplicity, but the critics are making a charge, and simplicity is not the complaint. Fashionable could be a criticism on its own, but it has no partner and does not follow from the explanation; mercurial means changeable.

questions.s: Though the composer's early quartets were long dismissed as _____ exercises, scholars now hear in them the first signs of his distinctive voice.
questions.e: "Dismissed" and "early" suggest the quartets were seen as immature, and "though" sets that against a later, kinder view. Callow (inexperienced and immature) and jejune (naive and simplistic) both fit. Masterly and virtuosic are synonyms of high praise, which no one would use to dismiss a work. Academic could also be dismissive, meaning merely dutiful, but it has no partner; pugnacious means combative.

questions.s: Mateo's colleagues found his _____ exasperating: he would agree to a plan in the morning and reject it by the afternoon.
questions.e: Agreeing in the morning and rejecting by afternoon shows a habit of changing his mind. Fickleness and inconstancy both mean that. Obstinacy and stubbornness are synonyms meaning refusal to change, the opposite. Impulsiveness could fit alone, since quick reversals can be rash, but it means acting without thought rather than changing allegiance, and it has no partner; erudition means great learning.

questions.s: Although the new manager was initially _____ about changing the shift schedule, she eventually agreed to it after reading the staff survey results.
questions.e: "Although" and "eventually agreed" signal that she first resisted the change, so the blank needs a word for unwillingness: hesitant and reluctant. Eager and keen are a synonym pair, but an eager manager would not need to be won over, so they reverse the contrast. Uninformed fits the mention of the survey, yet no other choice means the same thing, so it has no partner.

questions.s: The museum guide was praised for her _____ explanations, which made even complex paintings easy for young visitors to understand.
questions.e: The clause "which made even complex paintings easy ... to understand" restates the blank, so it must mean easy to follow: lucid (clearly expressed) and clear. Obscure and murky are synonyms meaning hard to understand, the opposite of the clue. Patient could describe a good guide, but it does not explain why the paintings became easy to grasp and has no partner among the choices.

questions.s: Because the drought had lasted for many months, supplies of fresh water in the region grew _____, and residents were asked to limit their use.
questions.e: A long drought causes water to run short, and residents are asked to save it, so the blank means insufficient: scarce and meager (small in amount). Abundant and plentiful are a matching pair, but they contradict both the cause and the result in the sentence. Expensive is a plausible effect of a drought, yet no other choice shares its meaning, so it cannot complete an equivalent pair.

questions.s: Critics found the author's second novel _____, complaining that its plot simply repeated the pattern of her first book.
questions.e: The critics complain that the plot "simply repeated the pattern" of the first book, so the novel lacks freshness: formulaic (built on a fixed pattern) and unoriginal. Innovative and inventive are synonyms, but they praise originality and contradict the complaint. Lengthy is a common criticism of novels, but it says nothing about repetition and has no partner.

questions.s: The diplomat's _____ reply avoided any firm commitment, leaving both delegations unsure of her government's position.
questions.e: A reply that "avoided any firm commitment" and left listeners unsure is evasive (avoiding a direct answer) or noncommittal (not revealing a position). Candid and frank are a synonym pair meaning openly honest, which would have made her position clear. Brief fits the grammar and could describe a vague answer, but a short reply can still be firm, and no other choice matches it.

questions.s: Early photographers needed their subjects to remain _____ for several seconds, since any movement during the long exposure would blur the image.
questions.e: The reason given, that "any movement" would blur the image, tells us the subjects had to stay without moving: motionless and still. Restless and fidgety are synonyms, but they describe exactly the movement the photographers wanted to avoid. Silent fits the scene of a sitter waiting, yet sound has no effect on a photograph and silent has no partner.

questions.s: Although the experiment's first results were _____, later trials produced consistent data that clearly confirmed the hypothesis.
questions.e: "Although" sets the first results against later data that "clearly confirmed" the hypothesis, so the first results must have been unclear: inconclusive and ambiguous (open to more than one reading). Definitive and decisive are a synonym pair, but they would remove the contrast. Delayed fits the time order of the sentence, but nothing else in the choices means late, so it has no partner.

questions.s: The founder was known for her _____ attitude toward risk, often launching products long before her competitors felt ready to do so.
questions.e: Launching products "long before her competitors felt ready" shows a willingness to take chances, so the blank means bold or daring. Timid and cautious are near-synonyms describing the opposite attitude, so they fail the clue. Casual can loosely fit an attitude toward risk, but it suggests carelessness rather than courage and has no partner among the choices.

questions.s: The village's economy is heavily _____ on tourism; when visitor numbers fall, nearly every business in the area suffers.
questions.e: The second clause explains that businesses suffer when tourists stay away, which means the economy needs tourism: dependent and reliant. Independent and autonomous are synonyms meaning self-sufficient, the reverse of what the semicolon clause shows. Focused also fits grammatically ("focused on tourism"), but it describes emphasis rather than need and no other choice matches it.

questions.s: The committee's report was so _____ that readers needed hours to find the few practical recommendations buried in its pages.
questions.e: Recommendations that take hours to find because they are "buried" point to a report with far too many words: verbose and long-winded. Concise and succinct are a synonym pair, but a brief report would make the recommendations easy to find. Technical could also slow readers down, yet it concerns difficulty rather than length, and no other choice matches it.

questions.s: Many birds that seem _____ to the city are in fact recent arrivals that moved in only a few decades ago.
questions.e: "In fact recent arrivals" corrects a mistaken impression, so the birds must seem to have always lived there: native and indigenous (originating in a place).
